subject: Computer Networking
title: Network Segmentation
description: Learn Network Segmentation in one minute.

hook.text: A hacker breaches one machine. If the entire network is flat, every other machine is now reachable. Game over.

buildup.text: Segmentation divides a network into isolated zones. Each zone has its own access rules and boundaries.

discovery.text: VLANs and subnets create logical boundaries. Firewalls between segments control what traffic can cross.

twist.text: The 2013 Target breach started in their HVAC vendor's network. Without segmentation, attackers reached payment systems.

climax.text: Microsegmentation goes further — isolating individual workloads. Even within a zone, lateral movement is restricted.

punchline.text: Segmentation limits the blast radius. One breach doesn't mean total loss.

quiz.question: What does network segmentation prevent?
options: Attackers moving freely across the entire network after a breach
Users from connecting to the internet

details.summary: Network segmentation divides a network into isolated zones so a breach in one area cannot spread to others. VLANs, firewalls, and access control lists create boundaries between segments. Critical assets like databases and payment systems are placed in heavily restricted segments.
details.whyItMatters: Segmentation is the most effective way to limit blast radius when an attacker breaches the network. It turns one large target into many small, isolated ones.
takeaways: Segmentation limits how far an attacker can move laterally
VLANs and firewalls create boundaries between network zones
Critical assets go in the most restricted segments

faq.question: What is micro-segmentation?
faq.answer: Micro-segmentation applies security policies at the individual workload level rather than the network level. Each server or container has its own security boundary. Even if two servers are on the same subnet, traffic between them is controlled. This is the finest-grained segmentation available.

faq.question: How do you design network segments?
faq.answer: Group resources by function and sensitivity: separate user workstations, servers, databases, and IoT devices into different segments. Apply the principle of least privilege between segments, allowing only the specific traffic each group needs. Start with broad segments and refine over time.
